edge_explainer: Somero makes the laser-guided machines that pour non-residential concrete slabs - warehouses and distribution centres above all. Its 2021-22 earnings were the e-commerce warehouse build-out. Operating profit has fallen from US$43.1m (2022) to US$13.9m (2025), -68%, while the US private commercial construction spending that drives it fell only 15% from its own 2023 peak and is still 44% above 2019. That 4.6x amplification is the whole story: Somero sells the capital good, so its earnings track the change in construction activity rather than its level, and roughly 2x operating leverage doubles the swing again. So the cheapness on the screen is not a discount to a stable business - it is what a capital-goods trough looks like, and the FCF yield and net-cash ratio the screen scored it on are themselves trough artifacts (capex ran 0.9% of sales versus 2.2% the prior year). The cycle did just turn: the 16-Jul-2026 trading update was the first upgrade in three years, and customer deposits on the balance sheet jumped 7x to $3.56m. But the tape already paid for it, the stock is 5% off its 52-week high, and the round-trip touch is 435bp. Two structural findings override the business call. First, the AIM line is a Regulation S line of a DELAWARE corporation - ISIN USU834501038 (the U-prefix CUSIP is the Reg S convention), IBKR's own description reads 'SOMERO ENTERPRISES INC- REGS', and the company's entire SEC history is one Form D from 2009. Under Rule 905 these are permanently restricted securities because the issuer is domestic. US law does not flatly bar a US person from buying on the LSE (a designated offshore securities market under Rule 902(b)), but the broker gates it, and IBKR's Reg S policy could not be verified - so executability is UNVERIFIABLE, which is not clean. Second, the shelf tagged this name country_incorp 'JE' (Jersey) with a 0% withholding edge worth 1500bp. That is REFUTED: the auditor's opinion says 'a Delaware corporation' and the company's own AIM Rule 26 page says 'United States of America'. Dividends are US-source from a US C-corporation, so there is no foreign withholding to avoid and the 0%-withholding structural-edge argument is worth exactly zero on this name. Related and unresolved: Somero withholds under the US non-resident-alien regime through a UK registrar into CREST depositary interests, so whether a US holder's W-9 survives the nominee chain or the chain defaults to 30% withholding is an open ~100bp/yr operational risk. Worth recording separately: this is a US operating company that files nothing with the SEC - no 10-K, no 10-Q, no XBRL, no Section 16, no SOX 404 - and, by its own statement, is not subject to the UK City Code on Takeovers and Mergers. Neither regime's protections apply. The financials themselves verify clean: net cash US$33.2m against zero borrowings (the screen's $30.3m conservatively deducts leases), no capital commitments in Note 12, and no defined-benefit pension at all - Note 7 is a 401(k). The worst signal in the file is capital allocation: the supplemental dividend was explicitly omitted 'in support of M&A Framework' and the ordinary was cut 40%, prompting a shareholder revolt and a live governance review of board composition and capital allocation, partly bought off with a buyback raised from $6m to $12m.
